subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a fail-closed response-gate API, and what trusted validator/tool-ledger/audit semantics should block or release final output?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing runtime seam, but the permanent behavior changes a security boundary, plugin API contract, config surface, and operator recovery model that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Versioned Response Gate
options.body: Approve a maintainer-led core/plugin API design with explicit validator trust, mandatory-tool ledger, retry/fallback, audit, and plugin-owned policy-pack boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Keep Existing Advisory Hooks
options.body: Leave current pre-tool, finalization revision, and outbound cancellation hooks as advisory primitives and document that strict response compliance is not guaranteed by core.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Policy Work
options.body: Pause this item until related tool-confirmation, outbound pre-send, fake-tool, and machine-policy issues converge on one authorization model.

recommendation.title: Design Versioned Response Gate
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-led core/plugin API design with explicit validator trust, mandatory-tool ledger, retry/fallback, audit, and plugin-owned policy-pack boundaries before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans product security defaults, final response delivery, and plugin/API compatibility, and prior issue review already routed this surface to product/security design.
